emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(needed_headroom)]) from thread_b (LL_RESERVED_SPACE reads the headroom field assuming it is not torn by a concurrent write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: both the tunnel xmit write and the output-path read are entirely lockless; there is no lock or ordering primitive on either side, so no serialize/order(g) establishes the single-access atomicity the reader assumes
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write to the same field -> data race (torn/unstable headroom read)

fix_maps_to: patch wraps the tunnel writes in WRITE_ONCE and the LL_RESERVED_SPACE / LL_RESERVED_SPACE_EXTRA helper reads in READ_ONCE -> makes the conflicting single access atomic; a tearing annotation, not a serialize/order/counts guarantee
recall_risk_notes: Object and sites are in the static surface, so the pair is findable and the category maps to atomic(single access)=data_race. But both sides are entirely lockless and needed_headroom is a best-effort sizing hint; the read carries no order intent beyond no-tearing, and there is no flag/semantic guard. The design wants a semantic order/atomicity intent, so the LLM is very likely to adjudicate this benign and reject it (precision pressure), or only a pure-syntactic-race detector would fire. The fix is annotation-only and does not map to serialize/order/counts.
